en: Heating a sealed aerosol spray can increases gas pressure inside, which can cause the metal container to explode.
Boiling tap water until it reaches a rolling boil kills harmful bacteria and makes it safe to drink.
Mixing liquid bleach with ammonia creates toxic chloramine gas, which is dangerous to breathe.
Pouring water on a hot cooking oil fire causes the water to instantly vaporize and spread the burning oil.
Chewing solid food into smaller pieces increases its surface area, helping stomach acids digest it faster.
Touching solid dry ice with bare hands causes severe frostbite because it rapidly sublimates into freezing carbon dioxide gas.
Shaking a liquid medicine suspension thoroughly before drinking ensures the solid drug particles are evenly mixed in the liquid.
Baking soda reacting with vinegar produces carbon dioxide gas, which displaces oxygen to safely extinguish small kitchen fires.
Rubber is an electrical insulator, so electricians wear rubber gloves to prevent dangerous electric currents from passing through their bodies.
Sweat evaporating from your skin absorbs heat, which physically cools your body down on a hot day.
Using an activated charcoal filter physically traps solid dirt particles and absorbs chemical impurities to clean drinking water.
Blowing air onto a campfire supplies extra oxygen gas, which makes the chemical burning reaction burn hotter and faster.
